transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-09-23 15:00 UTC; Duration: 62 minutes; Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Argon CTO), Liam O'Connor (Argon Sec Eng), Grace Park (Argon DevOps), Hannah Wu (Argon Procurement)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Auto intro — I'm Maya, AE on the account, and Diego and Samir from the SE team will walk through the technical options for tenant keys.
[00:12] Priya: Hi, thanks. Quick context — Argon runs across EU and US regions, compliance team needs FIPS 140-2/3 validated HSM, and legal wants proof keys never leave customer control for certain tenant classes.
[00:25] Diego: Yep, understood. Today we'll sketch two main patterns: REDWOOD-hosted KMS with BYOK (key import or key-wrap) and Private HSM connector where keys stay in your HSM and Redwood holds only wrapped/delegated material.
[00:37] Liam: When you say "wrapped", is that envelop encryption? Like we wrap model serving keys with our master key in the HSM?
[00:44] Samir: Exactly — envelope encryption. We create ephemeral serving keys, those are wrapped with the tenant key in your H S M via PKCS#11 or cloud H S M API, so the root key never leaves the HSM.
[00:58] Grace: Are there latency impacts for each token because of unwrap ops? We have tight p95 token latency SLOs.
[01:05] Diego: Good question. Unwrapping happens at key issuance time — we cache the unwrapped ephemeral key in the runtime's KV cache for subsequent requests, so per-token overhead is minimal. We do a rewrap/refresh on rotation or after pool restarts.
[01:21] Priya: Ok, how does emergency key revocation work? If we revoke a tenant key, will the service immediately stop decrypting prior caches?
[01:28] Samir: We implement a check on cache validation flags. If the key is revoked, the cache entries are marked stale and we fall back to a safe failure mode — requests fail closed or hit a fallback model depending on your policy. There is a short window where already-issued ephemeral keys could be valid until cache expiry.
[01:45] Liam: What's that window typically? Seconds, minutes?
[01:48] Diego: Configurable. You can set short TTLs for ephemeral keys (e.g., 5–30 seconds) to minimize exposure. There's a tradeoff with throughput because shorter TTL means more unwrap ops on cold starts.
[01:59] Priya: We want proof that the HSM path uses FIPS validated modules — which vendors do you support?
[02:06] Maya: We have connectors for Thales, Utimaco, and common cloud HSMs. We'll share a vendor compatibility matrix. Note: some enterprise customers run a proxy HSM in their VPC and we connect over an encrypted channel.
[02:19] Grace: Is the connection inside our VPC or do you host an agent?
[02:23] Samir: For Private deployment, the connector runs inside your network — either an agent or a sidecar with MTLS. For Redwood-hosted dedicated, we do a hybrid mode where wrapped keys are imported and the wrapped blobs are stored in our control plane but only accessible after your KMS approves the unwrap.
[02:38] Hannah: From procurement — any escrow or split custody required? Legal asks if Redwood can be a key escrow.
[02:44] Maya: By default we don't hold unwrapped tenant keys. We support split custody scenarios: escrow with a third-party (customer-owned or neutral escrow). We can sign an SOP for key escrow terms.
[02:54] Liam: What about logs — do you provide audit logs of key activity? We need immutable time-stamped records for key usage for audit.
[03:01] Diego: Yes, we emit key operation logs: key unwrap, wrap, rotation, import/export attempts, and access control changes. Logs can be pushed to your SIEM or stored in your S3 with retention policies. They include request id, principal, action, and timestamp.
[03:17] Priya: Are the logs tamper-evident? Chain-of-custody?
[03:20] Samir: We support append-only storage plus HMAC chain or integration with your logging HSM for signatures. We can also stream to your audit pipeline. We'll provide a sample redacted log so you can validate fields.
[03:33] Grace: On RBAC/SSO — how are key lifecycle ops gated? We use Okta and SAML.
[03:38] Diego: We integrate with SAML/Okta and map groups to Redwood RBAC roles. Admin-only key ops require an elevated role and we support MFA for key release. You can require a two-person approval for critical primitives.
[03:50] Priya: Two-person approval would be a hard requirement for production keys. Is that out-of-the-box?
[03:55] Maya: It's available as a policy. We can demo the 2-person workflow in the deep-dive.
[03:59] Liam: How about rotation cadence? Our security policy says 90-day rotation for tenant master keys. Does Redwood force rotation?
[04:06] Samir: We can automate key rotation on your schedule; for BYOK you control rotate/import. Redwood can enforce rotation windows and report noncompliance. For some tenants we recommend 30–90 days depending on classification.
[04:19] Priya: And backup/escape hatches — if your service is down, can we still decrypt data?
[04:24] Diego: If you maintain a copy or escrow of the wrapped keys and your HSM is reachable, you can perform on-prem decrypts. We document escape sequences; for Private installs you retain full control.
[04:36] Hannah: Legal wants SLA specifics around key handling — can you provide workflow docs and an incident playbook?
[04:41] Maya: Yes — next step we'll share SOC 2 artifacts, the incident runbook, and a redacted incident response example.
[04:47] Priya: One more — does envelope encryption mean model weights are ever encrypted with tenant keys?
[04:52] Samir: We don't re-encrypt the model weights per tenant. Typically we encrypt per-request payloads or ephemeral session material. Model weights remain in a protected model store; access controls restrict which tenant requests are routed to which model instance. If you need per-tenant model encryption, that's a custom pattern we can explore.
[05:07] Grace: Can Redwood run in our air-gapped environment for certain regulated tenants?
[05:11] Diego: Yes, Redwood Private supports on-prem packages. The HSM connector is local and the control plane can be a customer-managed instance.
[05:18] Priya: For the pilot we want to validate wrap/unwrap latency and audit events end-to-end. Can you simulate 1000 concurrent requests?
[05:25] Maya: Diego can run a latency sim; we'll return results and a recommended TTL configuration.
[05:30] Diego: We'll also show a failure injection where the HSM denies unwrap to validate fail-closed semantics.
[05:36] Liam: Nice. How do you handle cross-region keys and residency — can keys be constrained to EU only and block US region requests?
[05:42] Samir: Yes, we support regional residency. The routing policy will only route requests for EU-resident tenants to EU-only capacity; attempts to route to other regions are blocked or require explicit fallback.
[05:54] Priya: Any regulatory certifications you can share? SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001?
[05:59] Maya: We'll attach our latest SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certs, plus a summary of controls around key management.
[06:06] Grace: Is there a way to rotate keys without interrupting active sessions?
[06:10] Samir: Yes: we support staged rotation with dual-wrap period where both old and new unwrapped ephemeral keys are accepted for a short window while caches warm.
[06:20] Hannah: Procurement question — pricing impact for HSM integration? We expect some surcharge for agent/connector support and on-prem installs.
[06:26] Maya: Pricing will include a connector setup fee and recurring support fee for HSM maintenance. We'll provide an estimate in the follow-up.
[06:33] Diego: Technical note: we use re-wrap-on-attach — the key usage path for inference is: client request -> routing -> ephemeral serving key unwrapped in runtime -> token generation. Long running sessions will need refresh logic.
[06:47] Priya: Ok, that clarifies. A couple of clarifying questions from security: can you show evidence of key material never persisted in plaintext on Redwood-managed disks?
[06:56] Samir: We don't persist tenant master material in plaintext. Ephemeral unwrapped keys are held in memory with OS protections and zeroed on release. We'll share a whitepaper and a memory-handling blurb.
[07:07] Grace: Great. Last — integration path: what's the minimum effort to get to a small POC for one EU tenant class?
[07:12] Maya: Suggested POC: 1) exchange vendor details and network config, 2) deploy connector in your test VPC, 3) import a test wrapped key and run 1k req sim. Should be 2–4 weeks depending on approvals.
[07:24] Priya: We'll aim for that. Thanks.
[07:28] Maya: Recap — Redwood to share: HSM connector doc, PKCS#11 examples, SOC2/ISO artifacts, redacted logs, and Diego will schedule deep-dive. Argon to confirm HSM vendor and FIPS needs.
[07:42] Priya: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[07:45] Maya: Thanks, we'll follow up with calendar invites.

Auto sections: Questions captured: "Can we revoke keys immediately? How to prove FIPS usage and non-persistence of plaintext keys? What's the latency impact of unwrap?"

End of transcript.
